buildSystem: none; the course is driven by GitHub Actions on the learner's fork

extractor.reason: Courseware repository. No source code, no exported symbols, and no network-facing API contract (no OpenAPI/SDL/.proto, no route or handler definitions). Symbol extraction has no substrate, so regen-registry emits an empty baseline with an explicit no-substrate reason rather than a fabricated one, and api-diff reports NO-BASELINE. Phase 1 API-surface detection: negative.

verificationNote: This project has no build, typecheck or test command. Closure duty 2 (independently re-run build/typecheck/test) has no command to run here and MUST report NO-SUCH-COMMAND rather than claim a pass. The project's real verification surface is the five GitHub Actions workflows in .github/workflows, which only execute on a learner's fork in response to their course actions and cannot be run from this repository.

uiSurface.reason: No rendered user interface. The repository ships Markdown and PNG screenshots; nothing renders a UI that a viewport capture could verify. The Visual Evidence Mandate generates no wiring here and no ui-change workflow is codified.

capabilities.selectionNote: The five standard entries were selected. Every 'detected' entry is a server injected by this remote Claude Code session's harness, not configured via `claude mcp` and not present in a local session; each was evaluated against the Phase 3 hard gate (a) and none completes the sentence 'granted because this project has ___' for a courseware repository, so none is granted and none appears in the Installed Capability Register. The github MCP additionally fails criterion (d): ~90 tools of schema for work the `gh` CLI does at zero schema cost.

granted.name: semble
granted.purpose: Indexed hybrid search across the course prose and workflow YAML before any grep-and-read sweep; the enumeration workload (every step file referencing a given image, every workflow writing a given step) is exactly what it exists for.
granted.matched: The 5 step Markdown files and 5 Actions workflow files identified in Phase 1, which cross-reference each other and the images/ tree by name.
granted.fallback: Grep/Glob sweeps, which cost tokens but never correctness.

granted.name: context7
granted.purpose: Live documentation lookup for GitHub Actions syntax and the actions/* the course workflows pin.
granted.matched: The five .github/workflows files, which use actions/checkout and the GitHub Actions expression and permissions syntax (Phase 1).
granted.fallback: Targeted reads of the workflow files plus docs.github.com links already cited in the course prose.

granted.name: deepwiki
granted.purpose: Digest answers about the external GitHub repositories the workflows depend on, without pulling their source into context.
granted.matched: .github/dependabot.yml and the pinned third-party actions consumed by the five workflows (Phase 1).
granted.fallback: context7, or a targeted read of the action's own README.

grantsDeclined.name: serena
grantsDeclined.reason: Phase 3 Tool Assignment rubric, v3.6.1 precondition: Serena is granted ONLY where its language servers cover the project's primary language. This project's primary language is Markdown and YAML, both named in the spec's known-uncovered list. The grant would still cost its schema every session and silently degrade to file search, which semble already does better. semble is granted in its place. Recorded so a future run does not re-litigate this.

grantsDeclined.name: frontend-design
grantsDeclined.reason: Not installed (see capabilities.failures) and, independently, this project has no UI surface, so no agent's duties would invoke it.

failures.name: frontend-design
failures.symptom: Could not be installed. `/plugin` is unavailable in this remote Claude Code environment, and the bootstrap session's attempt to shell out to the plugin CLI was denied by the auto-mode permission classifier.
failures.diagnosis: Environment limitation, not a project or network fault. Skills cost zero context until invoked, so the absence is a pure capability loss with no ongoing tax. This project has no UI surface, so nothing here would have invoked it regardless.

failures.name: phaneslight-plugin-hooks
failures.symptom: The three enforcement hooks (hook-stamp-guard, hook-size-check, hook-ledger-status) are installed to .phaneslight/scripts/ and verified, but are NOT registered and will not fire.
failures.diagnosis: From v3.7.0 hook registration lives in the PhanesLight plugin's own hooks/hooks.json, not in the project's .claude/settings.json. This bootstrap ran from a clone of the plugin repository because `/plugin` is unavailable in this remote environment, so no plugin is enabled and nothing registers the hooks. The mechanical-enforcement layer (Section II, Procedure in Scripts, Judgment in Prompts) is therefore inert until the plugin is installed locally. The scripts themselves are correct and carry the project-root refusal, so they arm with no further work the moment the plugin is enabled.
failures.retry: In a local Claude Code session: /plugin marketplace add Aloim/phaneslightplugin && /plugin install phaneslight@phaneslight, then restart the session to arm the hooks.

notes.testTree: Phase 2.5 Step 1b (tests/ scaffolding) was deliberately not performed. This repository is courseware with no source code and no test runner; a tests/ tree here would be inert scaffolding. Recorded as a scope decision taken by the user at bootstrap, not as an omission.
notes.stampedTrees: stampedTrees is deliberately limited to the documentation root. The course content trees (.github/steps/, .github/workflows/) are NOT stamped: new-file applies the module stamp `# <module> | <description>` to non-docRoot targets, and in a learner-facing .md file that line renders as an H1 heading, corrupting the course content the repository exists to deliver. Guarding those trees would break the product to enforce a convention it does not need.
